rounds.question: Name a cause of the Civil War

answers.explanation: This is a cause of the Civil War — the central conflict was whether slavery would spread into western territories.
This is a cause of the Civil War — Southern states argued they had the right to secede; the Union disputed this.
This is a cause of the Civil War — Southern states seceded after Lincoln won without carrying a single Southern state.
This is a cause of the Civil War — the industrial North and the agricultural, slave-based South had clashing economic interests.
This is a cause of the Civil War — decades of political compromise over slavery collapsed in the 1850s.

rounds.question: Name something the Emancipation Proclamation did or did not do

answers.text: Freed enslaved people in Confederate states
answers.explanation: This is what the Emancipation Proclamation did — it freed enslaved people in rebel states, as a war measure.
This is an effect of the Emancipation Proclamation — it redefined the war's purpose, making European support for the Confederacy politically toxic.

answers.text: Did not free enslaved people in border states
answers.explanation: This is a limit of the Emancipation Proclamation — Lincoln excluded border states to keep them in the Union.

answers.text: Allowed Black men to join the Union Army
answers.explanation: This is a consequence of the Emancipation Proclamation — nearly 180,000 Black soldiers served in the USCT afterward.

answers.text: Was a war measure not a law
answers.explanation: This is the legal basis of the Emancipation Proclamation — Lincoln used his war powers as commander-in-chief, not Congress.

rounds.question: Name a Reconstruction amendment and what it guaranteed

answers.explanation: This is a Reconstruction amendment — it permanently abolished slavery throughout the United States in 1865.
This is a Reconstruction amendment — it made all people born in the US citizens and guaranteed equal protection.

answers.text: 15th Amendment gave Black men the vote
answers.explanation: This is a Reconstruction amendment — it prohibited denying the vote based on race, color, or prior servitude.
This is a Reconstruction amendment guarantee — the 14th Amendment's equal protection clause is the foundation of civil rights law.
This is a Reconstruction amendment guarantee — the 14th Amendment applied due process rights against state governments.

rounds.question: Name a way Reconstruction was undermined after 1877

answers.explanation: This is how Reconstruction was undermined — Southern states passed laws mandating racial separation in public life.
This is how Reconstruction was undermined — these devices effectively stripped Black men of the vote the 15th Amendment had given them.
This is how Reconstruction was undermined — the sharecropping system trapped formerly enslaved people in cycles of debt.
This is how Reconstruction was undermined — the Klan used violence to drive Black voters and officeholders from public life.
This is how Reconstruction was undermined — Hayes became president in exchange for withdrawing federal troops from the South.

rounds.question: Name a characteristic of slavery in the antebellum South

answers.text: Slavery passed from mother to child
answers.explanation: This is a feature of antebellum slavery — the 'partus' rule made the child's status follow the mother's, expanding slaveholder property.

answers.text: Enslaved people had no legal rights
answers.explanation: This is a feature of antebellum slavery — enslaved people were legally property; they could not own, marry, or testify in court.
This is a feature of antebellum slavery — the domestic slave trade routinely broke up families, which abolitionists highlighted.
This is a feature of antebellum slavery — state laws regulated every aspect of enslaved people's lives, including movement and literacy.
This is a feature of antebellum slavery — any sign of rebellion, from running away to learning to read, was harshly punished.

rounds.question: Name a goal or policy of Lincoln's Reconstruction plan

answers.explanation: This is Lincoln's Reconstruction philosophy — his 'malice toward none' approach prioritized quickly restoring the Union.
This is Lincoln's Reconstruction plan — states could rejoin when 10% of 1860 voters swore loyalty, far less than Radicals wanted.
This is Lincoln's Reconstruction position — he opposed treating Southern leaders as traitors, which Radical Republicans rejected.
This is Lincoln's Reconstruction goal — he wanted rapid reunion, not a prolonged period of federal occupation.
This is Lincoln's Reconstruction stance — he vetoed the Wade-Davis Bill, which set much harsher readmission requirements.
